subject: Status update: degraded responses on /v1/generate (us-west pool)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Aurelia Ops <ops@aurelia.com>, James Smith <j.smith@aurelia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Status update: degraded responses on /v1/generate (us-west pool)

Hi James / Aurelia Ops team —

We’re seeing an elevation in 5xx and slow responses for generation requests routed to our us-west inference pool (affecting paths under /v1/generate). Impact window started ~09:05 PT and our monitoring shows increased p50/p95 and an error spike affecting ~6% of requests for your account.

What we’ve posted to the status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-06-usw1-pool-degradation

What we’re doing right now:
- Routing: applying a targeted reroute of traffic away from the affected host group while preserving capacity in the us-west region.
- Autoscaling: temporarily increased reserved burst capacity for us-west to reduce queuing.
- Investigation: SREs are actively triaging kernel logs, KV-cache evictions, and recent deploys to the pool.

Immediate ask: If you can share any critical jobs or API routes that need priority routing, reply here and we’ll pin those tokens to the fallback pool while the mitigation is active.

Attachments: aurelia_error_rate_snapshot.png (overview of error spike by token)

From: James Smith <j.smith@aurelia.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Status update: degraded responses on /v1/generate (us-west pool)

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the heads up.

We have some synchronous user flows that fall back to a degraded experience when generation fails; those are currently seeing failures (orders of magnitude more than baseline). Priority routes: /v1/generate/chat and /v1/generate/summary. If you can pin those, that will reduce user-visible errors.

ETA question: any rough ETA on mitigation stability? We’ve already paused a couple of high-throughput jobs.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Status update: degraded responses on /v1/generate (us-west pool)

Quick internal note — triage summary:
- Trigger: Canary deploy at 08:58 PT introduced a routing weight misconfiguration for a host shard serving cached KV prefixes; under typical load this causes increased KV eviction churn, which amplifies tail latency and leads to a higher rate of retries and downstream 502s.
- Mitigation applied 09:14 PT: adjusted routing weights to shift affected traffic to alternative shard and enabled temporary burst pools. Initial telemetry shows error rate dropping from ~6% -> ~1.2% for routed customers.
- Action plan: rollback the canary (targeted rollback scheduled at 10:15 PT) and run a post-rollback soak with additional telemetry checks.

I’ve attached a draft postmortem (postmortem-draft-v1.docx). After rollback we’ll escalate a final postmortem to status and commit to action items: tighter canary throttle, automated divergence alerts for routing weights, and an improved KV eviction metric.

cc: @on-call (Sean) for confirmation of rollback start and finish times.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-v1.docx

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Aurelia Ops <ops@aurelia.com>, James Smith <j.smith@aurelia.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Resolved: us-west pool degraded responses — follow-up and postmortem link

Hi James / Aurelia team —

Thanks for the quick coordination. We rolled back the canary at 10:18 PT; the routing adjustment and burst capacity reduced request errors and we've observed normalizing latency and error rates over the afternoon. Final impact window: 09:05 PT — 10:40 PT with residual noise through ~13:00 PT for a small subset of sessions.

What we fixed:
- Rolled back problematic canary and restored prior routing weights.
- Applied temporary pinned routing for your priority endpoints (/v1/generate/chat and /v1/generate/summary) during the remediation window.
- Tuned KV eviction thresholds to reduce immediate tail amplification.

Customer-visible metrics: your error rate peaked at ~6% and returned to baseline (<0.5%) by 13:10 PT. We’ll share a token-level break down if helpful.

Postmortem and next steps: we published a full incident post to the status page (link below) including the timeline and action items. We’re scheduling a 30-minute sync with your platform team next week to review the postmortem and any compensating actions you’d like. Please reply with preferred times.

Status and postmortem: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-06-usw1-pool-degradation

Attachments: postmortem-draft-v1.docx

—
Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
